A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EMD and contain readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting reliable comparison. All supplied pages were inspected: v1 ends with references, while v2 includes supplementary Sections A-E.

before.justification: v1 reports original EMD reconstruction, novel-view synthesis and component-ablation results on Waymo in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3-5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments with additional frameworks, KITTI, shifted camera trajectories and embedding dimensions.

M1.justification: v1 states that it uses the baseline losses; v2 introduces neighboring-embedding smoothness and deformation regularization. v2 also adds DeSiRe-GS position/color deformation and OmniRe SMPL pose/shape refinement, and replaces StreetGaussian's additive rotation correction with ordered rotation composition. These are substantive procedural changes beyond the retained motion embeddings and coarse/fine architecture.

E1.justification: The original Waymo coverage is retained, and KITTI is added. Section 5.3 also evaluates genuinely new camera trajectories shifted left and right by 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 meters, extending evaluation beyond interpolated views along the recorded trajectory.

E2.justification: The original S3Gaussian and StreetGaussian comparison sets remain. New Tables 2 and 4 add reported comparisons involving DeSiRe-GS, OmniRe, S-NeRF, StreetSurf, SUDS, PVG, DeformGS and HUGS, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: New experiments use four Waymo and three KITTI scenes for the DeSiRe-GS comparison, add a three-camera StreetGaussian setting alongside the original one-camera setting, and evaluate human regions with OmniRe. v2 also introduces FPS and a trajectory-shift protocol using FID against original-trajectory images. Newly disclosed training settings alone do not establish changes to retained experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Table 8 add sensitivity experiments varying Gaussian embedding dimensions across 8/32/128 and temporal dimensions across 1/4/16, including parameter costs. Section 5.3 adds tests of generalization away from the recorded camera trajectory. The original component-removal ablations and motion-deformation comparison are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original component-ablation scores are unchanged. The StreetGaussian+EMD row is revised: full-image PSNR changes from 36.03 to 35.41 and vehicle PSNR from 29.81 to 30.96. v1 describes reconstruction whereas v2 explicitly labels novel-view synthesis, so a same-setting performance change is not established. Substantial new results include DeSiRe-GS, OmniRe, sensitivity tests and trajectory FID, such as 83.48 versus 45.11 at the 0.5-meter offset in v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation receives localized revisions: v1 Equation 14 sums rotation corrections, while v2 Equation 13 composes them multiplicatively. v2 also supplies explicit SMPL-refinement and neighboring-embedding regularization equations. No theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes a broadly applicable module providing reconstruction improvements in supervised and self-supervised settings. v2 makes self-supervised motion modeling the primary contribution, treats supervised use as an extension, claims the first such plug-and-play module, and explicitly claims state-of-the-art self-supervised novel-view synthesis on Waymo and KITTI. These strengthen and refocus the headline scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of DeSiRe-GS and OmniRe improvements, explains the inadequacy of trajectory interpolation for assessing simulation, and discusses embedding-capacity versus computational-cost tradeoffs. The original component-ablation interpretations remain. The lighting limitation is unchanged and merely moves from Section 6 to Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 supplies embedding dimensions, interpolation details, regularization settings, loss coefficients, LiDAR initialization and filtering, Adam training budgets, warm-up procedures and A800 hardware information. It changes the code statement from a future release to stated availability. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although v1's explicit every-tenth/every-fourth-frame evaluation intervals are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 centers DeSiRe-GS and OmniRe in its positioning and presents EMD as filling a specifically self-supervised motion-modeling gap. It removes the directly relevant Bae et al. discussion of embeddings for fast/slow motion while introducing stronger priority claims. Section 2 also changes EmerNeRF's characterization from flow-free in v1 to optical-flow-guided in v2.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, preliminaries, supervised-results discussion and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting or condensation. The method gains finer subsection organization, the experimental narrative is reorganized, and limitations move into the new supplementary structure. These exceed incidental wording changes accompanying added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for DeSiRe-GS, OmniRe, trajectory FID, loss coefficients and embedding sensitivity, plus a new lane-change figure. The StreetGaussian table gains camera-setting blocks. The original ablation figure moves from Figure 5 to Figure 6 and adds pedestrian zooms to retained images; typography, spacing and figure placement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1's broad applicability claim relied on two frameworks evaluated only on Waymo, with little implementation documentation. v2 substantially strengthens that evidence through additional representations, KITTI and off-trajectory evaluation, while examining inference cost and embedding sensitivity. Its training specifications and corrected rotation composition also improve technical inspectability. Omitted holdout intervals and reduced discussion of relevant embedding-based prior work weaken reporting and positioning, but the gains in applicability evidence and reproducibility outweigh these shortcomings.
